result.title: ViewDreamer: A Robot World Model beyond Fixed Camera Setups
result.summary: Video generation models are increasingly important for robot learning, yet most generate each camera view separately or tile all views in a fixed layout. Robot demonstrations, however, are captured by synchronized cameras whose number, placement, and order vary across embodiments. We present ViewDreamer, a single world model that handles variable sets of cameras by disentangling per-view generation from cross-view interaction. Each view follows the generation path of a pretrained single-view model, and views interact only through shared slot tokens. We stabilize multi-view training with a curriculum that gradually increases the number of views. Cross-View Slot Agreement uses visual foundation models to group geometrically and semantically similar regions across views into shared slots. On RoboView-Bench, which covers one to four cameras, ViewDreamer achieves the best generation quality among the models evaluated and improves cross-view consistency over independent per-view generation. These gains carry over to our world-action model (WAM) and action-conditioned world model (AC-WM). Our WAM outperforms the FastWAM-Joint baseline on LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin 2.0, and RoboDojo, and on a real Franka robot. Both variants improve out-of-domain generalization to various camera settings and scenes.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ViewDreamer 机器人世界模型，将可变数量相机的视频生成拆成「单视图独立生成 + 通过共享 slot token 跨视图交互」，并用逐步增加视图数的课程训练，在 RoboView-Bench 上评估生成质量与跨视图一致性。
AI.relevance_reason: 共享 slot token 作为多视图信息的紧凑瓶颈，可供核查 LVR 中跨视图证据聚合与任务必要视觉细节是否被保留；其「视图数递增课程」也可能与长度泛化有关，但原论文面向机器人世界模型生成，与推理期 latent 状态的关系仅为推测。
